# Test 20261006-165102-d6e7: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:5; app.py:27; app.py:59; state.json:14 | `shop.refund` received `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `{"refund": "RF-C3E5A9", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}`. The rule says, “A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it.” The code compares `args["amount_eur"] > APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS`, where `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so this €80 refund bypassed approval. The saved order contains the paid refund and no approval request. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:10; trace.jsonl:13; trace.jsonl:17; state.json:16 | The reply claims “the amount has been paid back to your card.” The tool result reports only the refund ID, amount and `"status": "paid"`; neither the rules nor the saved refund identifies a card or payment destination. Turn 3 repeats the unsupported destination claim: “has been processed and sent to your card.” |

## Notes

The transcript reports: “Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test.” Reviewed all three turns and all 18 model items, findings.json, audit.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, and the current state.json using read-only commands. Findings contains no findings; the audit reports no breaks, errors, or blocked calls. The order lookup and refund amount match the tester's requests. The current state contains refund RF-C3E5A9 for €80 on order 5120, consistent with the tool's paid result, but inconsistent with the manager-approval rule.

No app was started, no message was sent to it, and no state was changed. Only this report was written. No project tests or additional business-rule documents were found. Actual card settlement, delivery dates, customer identity, and any external manager activity cannot be verified from the available records and project state; no additional violations are inferred from those gaps.
